messages.content: first satellite compared to the latest

message.content:
The **first satellite** was **Sputnik 1**, launched by the Soviet Union on October 4, 1957; it was about the size of a beach ball, weighed **83.6 kg (183.9 lb)**, and carried only batteries, a radio transmitter, and antennae.[2][1] By contrast, the **latest satellites** are much more advanced and mission-specific, and recent missions include large, sophisticated spacecraft such as **Spektr-R**, described as a **10-meter radio dish** used in a space-based telescope system.[1]

A simple comparison:

| Feature | First satellite: Sputnik 1 | Latest satellites in the results |
|---|---|---|
| Launch era | 1957[2] | Modern era, including later missions such as Spektr-R[1] |
| Size | About a beach ball, 58 cm in diameter[2] | Can be far larger and more specialized, such as a 10-meter radio dish[1] |
| Mass | 83.6 kg (183.9 lb)[2] | Not given in the results for the latest examples |
| Purpose | Demonstrated that an artificial satellite could orbit Earth; no scientific payload[2] | Scientific observation and advanced space-based astronomy[1] |
| Impact | Marked the start of the Space Age[2] | Part of the mature era of satellite science and exploration[1] |

If you meant **“latest satellite” as the most recently launched one**, the provided results do not identify a single newest satellite, so I can only compare Sputnik 1 to later, more advanced examples mentioned in the sources.[1][2]
